summary: The bill eliminates all federal preferences, programs, and references based on race or gender for farmers and ranchers by striking every mention of 'socially disadvantaged' producers from agricultural statutes and barring the USDA from granting any such preferences in its programs.

scores.thoughts: The bill removes statutory references to 'socially disadvantaged farmers and ranchers' and bars race/gender preferences in USDA programs. It does not alter overall funding levels, authorize new appropriations, or rescind existing spending authority, so it has no bearing on government spending.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
The legislation is confined to agricultural statutes and contains nothing related to health insurance, medical care delivery, or public/private healthcare systems.
No references to firearms, Second Amendment issues, or gun regulations appear in the bill.
The bill does not touch immigration law, border policy, visas, or protections for non-citizens.
No provisions relate to reproductive health services or abortion access.
The legislation is limited to USDA programs and contains no defense or military spending provisions.

While the bill amends several conservation-title sections, the changes are strictly limited to deleting 'socially disadvantaged' eligibility language; the underlying environmental standards and funding mechanisms remain unchanged.
Farm-program preferences are distinct from means-tested welfare entitlements such as SNAP or TANF; the bill does not alter eligibility or benefit levels for those programs.
No education policy, school funding, or school-choice provisions are present.
The bill does not address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No criminal-sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation measures are included.
The legislation contains no tariff, trade-agreement, or import/export provisions.
No deficit-reduction targets, debt-ceiling language, or fiscal-rule changes are present.
The bill addresses race and gender preferences only; it does not mention sexual orientation or gender identity.
No foreign-assistance or international-development provisions appear.
The bill is silent on voting rights, election administration, or voter-ID requirements.
No technology, data-privacy, or platform-regulation content is included.
The legislation does not address collective bargaining, union rights, or labor standards.
The bill prohibits race- and gender-based preferences in USDA programs but does not reference religious exemptions or civil-rights enforcement mechanisms.
